title: Staying in private homes; Atmore, Alabama 1926
summary: Riddick recalls a fried-chicken dinner in Atmore, Alabama, on his first band job in 1926.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah. We were talking about your being on the road in places like Texas. Did you ever stay in private homes?

Once in a great while we'd play a big affair at a private home and stay there that night. Homes big enough all up in northern Alabama and all over everywhere. Atmore, Alabama, we did that. That was in the first band I played in, in Atmore, Alabama. We went up there. One of the boys were in the band. Bobby Swartz was in love with a girl up there. And her family invited us to come up there to a big fried chicken dinner. And we sat down to the table and there was just stacks and stacks and stacks of fried chicken on the table. But no knives and forks on the plates. And I looked around and the mother says, oh, don't worry about knives and forks. Everybody else does too. Look for it. You eat this chicken with your hands. If you can't, you just leave the table. Never forget that in Atmore, Alabama. And that was in 1926. That was the time that I got my first piano job in a band. Because I played drums five years before that.
